key_insight: IMPACT combines inverter-level cloud dynamics with plant history and physical solar signals to improve probabilistic photovoltaic generation forecasts 10–110 minutes ahead.
engineering_relevance: More accurate, calibrated near-term PV forecasts could support grid scheduling and storage dispatch rather than directly improve solar-cell efficiency.
method: Encode plant history, inverter-level spatial dynamics, future solar geometry, and current weather in four branches fused through gated cross-attention.
Use learned graph adjacency and horizon-weighted cloud heterogeneity and inverter ramp-down signals.
Learn horizon-conditioned corrections to smart persistence, then calibrate quantiles online with kernel-weighted adaptive conformal calibration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance above all 14 baselines, with FSS 0.2950—0.099 above the next-best model—and FSS 0.198 under overcast skies and 0.255 under variable skies; every branch contributed positively in ablation.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset scale or cross-site validation, leaving generalization to other PV plants uncertain.
paper_title: IMPACT: Inverter-Informed Multimodal Learning for Photovoltaic Generation Forecasting
